To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

public multi-touch displays are used in a variety of social configurations that include parallel, sequential, and collaborative interactions; that the social organization of interaction at a public display is achieved through a complex interplay between the affordances of the technology and the social practices of the users; and that the social organization at a public display can be used to create new social spaces.

public multi-touch displays are used in a variety of ways that are not found in private settings, and that these uses are enabled and shaped by the display size, the multi-touch feature, and the social organization of interaction.

public use of a large multi-touch wall display is characterized by: (1) a social organization that enables the use by multiple people at once, (2) a high degree of parallelism in the use, (3) an emphasis on social interaction rather than on the content of the application, and (4) a tendency for users to mark the display as theirs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of public displays for urban settings, and with the social organization of interaction with such displays.
the social organization of public displays in urban environments, and the role of the display in the social life of the city.
the design of public displays in a way that supports social interaction and the use of public space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CityWall system is not a "public display" in a conventional sense, but an urban phenomenon in its own right.
the CityWall is a social space, a public space, and a space for public display.
public displays are not just public, but also very social.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
public displays are social artifacts that can become part of the social fabric of the urban space, but that their use requires careful design and social negotiation.
the use of a multi-touch display in public space is a social phenomenon, and the design and deployment of such a display should consider social aspects.
the public space is an active and social space, where people are constantly negotiating and redefining the rules for the usage of the space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a public display is not simply a device, it is a social space.
public multi-touch displays can become social objects, which are not only used by individuals, but also appropriated by groups and crowds.
a public multi-touch display is a social space, not merely an interface.
